text:
Jordan (CS): Hey team — Enterprise customer (CUST-482, EU region) reporting huge latency and unexpected token billing spikes. They say traffic appears to be routed to us-west. Repro steps and captures below, please advise.

Jordan (CS): Repro curl they ran:
```
curl -i https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-live-REDACTED\" \
  -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":16}'
```
Response headers (from customer):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-redwood-region: us-west-2
x-request-id: req_0a1b2c
content-length: 543
latency-ms: 420
```

Jordan (CS): Traceroute from their office (Paris ISP MobiTel):
```
traceroute to api.redwood.ai (13.224.0.1)
 1  10.0.0.1 ...
 6  their-resolver.mobi.eu (82.45.12.1)
 8  cloudflare-gw-us.example.net (104.16.32.1)  180 ms
```

Maya (Support): :eyes: do they have an example request id we can look up? Also any timestamp for the billing spike?

Jordan (CS): Billing spike 2026-03-09 09:12-09:40 UTC, matched the latency reports. Request id above (req_0a1b2c) is from their sample. They also attached a tcpdump showing no EDNS-Client-Subnet (ECS) in the query and the resolver IP looks US-based to our geoip: 82.45.12.1 -> mapped wrong region in our DB.

Eric (SRE): Quick hypothesis: either our GeoIP DB entry for that ISP got wrong country/region mapping, or the customer's ISP is egressing via a US transit and the resolver IP is being geolocated to US. Could also be EDNS strip by the resolver causing upstream cache to choose a wrong anycast pop.

Eric (SRE): Can we get the x-origin-resolver-ip and EDNS info from the customer? Ask them to run:
```
dig +short @82.45.12.1 api.redwood.ai ANY +noedns
dig +short @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.ai +short +bufsize=4096 +edns=0
```

Jordan (CS): Requested those outputs. Customer provided one: `82.45.12.1` resolves to their ISP; dig against 8.8.8.8 returns our EU A record but their local resolver trace shows Cloudflare hop in the US.

netops-bot: geoip-sync job: last run 2078897000, status=FAILED, error=S3 500 (retry queued)

Maya (Support): Hmm netops-bot shows a failed geoip sync earlier — could be related. Lia, do we have any rollout or GeoIP DB update around 2078896xxx?

Lia (Prod Eng): Checking deploy logs... deploy-bot shows geoip update attempts:
```
deploy-bot: geoip-update v2026-03-07 -> START 2078896000
deploy-bot: geoip-update v2026-03-07 -> ERROR S3 500 2078897000
deploy-bot: geoip-update v2026-03-07 -> RETRY SUCCESS 2078899800
```
Looks like there was a window where older DB still in use. We pushed a retry but some edge caches may have stale copies.

Eric (SRE): That fits. If an edge had the old mapping it could hand out US pop addresses to EU resolvers. We should confirm which edge nodes served req_0a1b2c. Jordan, can you pull the request-id lookup from our logs and paste the edge hostname?

Jordan (CS): Retrieved from logs: req_0a1b2c -> edge-host-nyc-03. So request was processed by NYC edge. Customer says they didn't change DNS.

Eric (SRE): Actionable mitigation for customer: ask them to use 1.1.1.1 or 8.8.8.8 to see if resolver route changes, and temporarily add header X-Region: eu-west-1 in their integration to pin EU region while we investigate. Note: we need to confirm region pinning works for that account (some orgs locked to hosted routing).

Jordan (CS): Customer tried X-Region but got 401 earlier when they set it manually (they're on a managed Dedicated plan? unclear). Also reported that TTL on their resolver is 300s; some ISP caches may be much longer.

Maya (Support): For support playbook: 1) collect dig +trace, 2) collect request ids and edge hostnames, 3) confirm geoip db version on edge host, 4) offer workaround (use public resolver / region pin header) and escalate to eng-infra.

Lia (Prod Eng): I'll open infra incident. Immediate tasks assigned: 
- Confirm which edges had stale geoip v (edge-host-nyc-03 shows old mapping)
- Invalidate GeoIP cache on EU edges and force a reload from S3
- Add telemetry to log resolver EDNS presence and resolver IP for future debug
- Reach out to customer with suggested resolvers and ask for local traceroute after DNS flush

Eric (SRE): Also we should consider changing prefill TTL for EU A records to lower value for the next 24h while we remediate, to reduce sticky misroutes. Lia, can infra do a short TTL push?

Lia (Prod Eng): Yes, I'll coordinate with DNS ops. Pushing TTL 60 for eu-prefill for 1 hour.

netops-bot: geoip-sync job: retry run 2078899800 -> OK, new db v2026-03-15 deployed

Jordan (CS): Customer confirmed after switching to 1.1.1.1 latency dropped from ~420ms to 32ms and region header now eu-west-1. They're testing TTL flush now.

Maya (Support): Great, please keep notes on the billing spike timeframe; finance may need the request id list for credits.

Jordan (CS): Will collect request ids and send through escalation template. Thanks everyone.

Lia (Prod Eng): Incident created: INC-2026-345 (GeoIP sync window caused EU->US misrouting for some ISP resolvers). Owner: Lia. Will post updates in #incidents.

Eric (SRE): Follow-ups: add automated alert when geoip-sync fails, and add dashboard for resolver-country mismatch rate.

Jordan (CS): Customer happy with workaround for now, laying low until TTLs propagate. Closing loop with them once infra confirms cache invalidation. :white_check_mark:
